content: 1. Administer 1 gram (600 mg base) of chloroquine orally once daily for 2 days, followed by 500 mg (300 mg base) once daily for 14 to 21 days. 2. As of June 15, 2020, the FDA revoked the Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for chloroquine. 3. The FDA determined that chloroquine is unlikely to be effective in treating COVID-19 for the authorized uses in the EUA. 4. The FDA cited ongoing serious cardiac adverse events and other potential serious side effects, concluding that the known and potential benefits of chloroquine no longer outweigh the known and potential risks for the EUA. 5. Additional clinical trials may continue to evaluate potential benefits, but the FDA deemed the EUA no longer appropriate. 6. The NIH COVID-19 Treatment Guidelines recommend against the use of chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine, with or without azithromycin, for the treatment of COVID-19 in both hospitalized and non-hospitalized patients. 7. Chloroquine decreases the effects of agalsidase alfa and agalsidase beta due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. These combinations are contraindicated. 8. Artemether increases the toxicity of chloroquine by prolonging the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the toxicity of chloroquine by prolonging the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Chloroquine increases the levels of eliglustat by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 12. If co-administered with strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, reduce the eliglustat dose from 84 mg twice daily to 84 mg once daily in extensive and intermediate metabolizers. Eliglustat is contraindicated if strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors are given concomitantly with strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 13. Lefamulin increases the level or effect of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 14. Lefamulin is contraindicated with CYP3A substrates known to prolong the QT interval. 15. Mavorixafor increases the level or effect of chloroquine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 16. Mavorixafor, a strong CYP2D6 inhibitor, is contraindicated with drugs highly dependent on CYP2D6 for clearance. 17. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of pazopanib by prolonging the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Quinidine increases the level or effect of chloroquine through other mechanisms. This combination is contraindicated. 19. Quinidine is contraindicated in patients receiving drugs that both prolong the QT interval and are metabolized by CYP2D6, such as chloroquine. 20. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of voriconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 21. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of amiodarone by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Chloroquine and amisulpride both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administered. 23. Chloroquine increases the level or effect of amlodipine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Chloroquine and anagrelide both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Apalutamide decreases the level or effect of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Co-administration of apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, with drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates can result in lower exposure to these medications. Avoid or substitute another drug when possible. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect if medication must be co-administered. Adjust dose according to prescribing information if needed. 27. Chloroquine increases the level or effect of aripiprazole by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Aripiprazole and chloroquine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of arsenic trioxide by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Avoid use with CYP2D6 substrates where minimal increases in concentration may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. 39. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Eribulin and chloroquine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If concurrent use is necessary, ECG monitoring is recommended. 50. Fexinidazole will increase the level or effect of chloroquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4. Co-administration may increase the risk for adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 51. Fingolimod and chloroquine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 52. If unable to avoid co-administration, obtain ECGs when initiating, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold if QTc interval >500 ms or a change from baseline >60 ms. 54. Givosiran will increase the level or effect of chloroquine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of sensitive CYP2D6 substrates with givosiran. If unavoidable, decrease the CYP2D6 substrate dosage in accordance with approved product labeling. 55. Chloroquine and glasdegib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of QTc interval prolongation. 56. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 59. Immunosuppressive drugs may reduce the immune response to influenza vaccine. 60. Inotuzumab and chloroquine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unable to avoid concomitant use, obtain ECGs and electrolytes before and after initiation of any drug known to prolong QTc, and periodically monitor as clinically indicated during treatment. 61. If alternative therapy cannot be used, exercise caution and consider a dose reduction of the CYP2D6 substrate. 102. Albuterol and chloroquine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 103. Aluminum hydroxide will decrease the level or effect of chloroquine by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Use caution and monitor. Separate doses by at least 4 hours. 104. Aluminum hydroxide will decrease the level or effect of chloroquine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Use caution and monitor.
